title: Commonly confused pairs
note: In each pair the wrong option is usually the twin's meaning. Venal is for sale (Latin venum, sale); venial is pardonable (venia, forgiveness). A speaker implies; a listener infers. You flout a rule but flaunt a new watch. Discreet means tactful; discrete means separate. Tortuous means twisting; torturous means painful.

items.a: open to bribery; corrupt
items.ex: A venal inspector signed off on the bridge in exchange for cash.

items.a: minor and forgivable, of a fault or sin
items.ex: Forgetting her birthday was a venial sin; forgetting the wedding was not.

items.a: to suggest without stating directly
items.ex: Are you implying that I ate the last slice?

items.a: to conclude from evidence or reasoning
items.ex: From the wet umbrellas, she inferred it had started raining.

items.a: to openly disregard a rule or convention
items.ex: Drivers flout the speed limit on that stretch every morning.

items.a: to display ostentatiously
items.ex: He flaunted his new watch by checking the time every minute.

items.a: to refer to indirectly
items.ex: The speech alluded to the scandal without naming anyone.

items.a: to escape or evade, often skillfully
items.ex: The fox eluded the hounds by doubling back through the creek.

items.a: to suppress or remove objectionable material
items.ex: The network censored two words from the broadcast.

items.a: to express severe formal disapproval of
items.ex: The Senate voted to censure the senator for misconduct.

items.a: to draw out a response or information
d: to forbid by law or custom
items.ex: The teacher's question elicited a long silence.

items.a: forbidden by law, rule, or custom
items.ex: Police seized a truck full of illicit fireworks.

items.a: careful not to cause offense or reveal secrets
items.ex: A discreet assistant, she never repeated what she heard in meetings.

items.a: separate and distinct
items.ex: The project breaks into three discrete phases.

items.a: full of twists and turns; needlessly complex
items.ex: A tortuous mountain road wound up to the monastery.

items.a: causing great pain or suffering
items.ex: The final mile of the march was torturous in the heat.

items.a: harmful or unfavorable
items.ex: The drug had few adverse effects.

items.a: having a strong dislike or opposition
items.ex: She is not averse to a little risk.

items.a: to struggle clumsily or in confusion
items.ex: The witness floundered when asked for the exact time.

items.a: to sink, or to fail completely
items.ex: The ship foundered in the storm with all hands.

items.a: hard to find, catch, or achieve
items.ex: A perfect score proved elusive.

items.a: based on illusion; not real
items.ex: The savings were illusory once shipping costs were added.

items.a: an inscription in memory of a person buried
d: a short quotation opening a book
items.ex: His epitaph read simply, "He kept bees."

items.a: a descriptive word or phrase, often disparaging
d: a list of a book's errors
items.ex: Richard I earned the epithet "the Lionheart."

items.a: famous and respected in a field
items.ex: An eminent surgeon led the panel.

items.a: to decrease in value
d: to grow in value over time
items.ex: A new car depreciates the moment it leaves the lot; to deprecate, by contrast, is to disapprove.

items.a: to order or direct as a rule or remedy
items.ex: The rules prescribe a two-minute penalty for tripping.

items.a: a mournful poem, especially a lament for the dead
d: a speech praising someone at a funeral
items.ex: Gray's "Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard" mourns the forgotten poor.

items.a: impartial; free of personal stake
items.ex: A disinterested referee has no bet on the game, though she may care deeply about it.

items.a: puzzled or bewildered
items.ex: The tourists looked bemused by the rules of cricket.

items.a: to be a powerful factor against or for
items.ex: His long absences militated against a promotion.

items.a: clever, original, and inventive
items.ex: An ingenious hinge let the table fold into the wall.
